SOC stock in bulk soils is not significantly influenced by the climatic gradient, but SOC in aggregate fractionation is sensitive to the climatic gradient with a higher SOC stock in temperate regions than in tropical regions.
the stock of SOC was higher in topsoils and Haplic Luvisols and Rhodi Humus Ferrosols in the temperate and tropical regions, respectively.

the SOC stock and stability were mainly controlled by climate and soil texture in central south China, and that the zonal variation in the SOC stock was mainly due to HMr in temperate regions and HAs in tropical regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SOC stock in topsoil and subsoil was significantly affected by climatic factors (temperature and precipitation), and the SOC was primarily stored in the HMr fraction, which decreased along the climatic gradients.
the stock of SOC in topsoil was significantly higher in the temperate region than in the tropical region, but the stock of SOC was higher in the tropical region in subsoil.

the stock and distribution of SOC were significantly associated with the soil properties, which could provide a reference for the management of soil carbon and the prediction of soil carbon sequestration in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SOC stock and its distribution in the soil profile were highly dependent on the climatic conditions.
the SOC stock and stability in zonal soils of central south China was significantly affected by the climatic gradient, which is of great importance to the global carbon budget.

the SOC stock in soils is mainly determined by the HMr and HA, and the HMr and HAs stock is closely related to soil pH and clay mineralogy, which is consistent with the hypothesis of the importance of soil clay and pH in the formation of SOC.
